To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and analyzed 10, 000 Android application projects from GitHub, and found that the most common power management activities performed by Android app developers are: 1) to use the PowerManager to manage power state; 2) to use a wake-lock to keep the device from sleeping; 3) to use a partial wake-lock to allow a device to wake up to handle some specific tasks; 4) to use the WakefulBroadcastReceiver to wake the device when it is sleeping
We mined 3, 000 Android applications and found that 1, 000 applications have power management commits, and we identified 20 common power management tasks that are used by developers.

(1) developers use a wide range of strategies to manage power, and (2) these strategies can be categorized into 4 major categories, i.e., (a) using the system, (b) using the device, (c) using the application and (d) using the network.
